messages.author: e049f93a4d6ba7b3
messages.subject: Area delimitation and model testing
parts:
Hi everybody,

I have a rather simple issue which I have trouble resolving: How to
compare different area delimitations?

Specifically, I suspect that subdividing one of my tip ranges would
better explain range evolution, as different subareas seem to have
different histories. I thought testing this statistically would be
straightforward, I would just compare the performance of different
"area subdivision models" – but then I thought, is the area
delimitation actually part of my _model_ or am I rather changing the
information in my _data_ when I change area delimitation? In that
case, I couldn't do any statistical model comparison...

This might be obvious, but I can't figure it out. Can anyone help?

Thanks in advance,

Jan

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: Area delimitation and model testing
parts:
Hi!  I am deep in revisions, but briefly: This is a deep question that I have also thought about.  Your statements are correct about changing the model vs. changing the data.  I feel the question needs some serious thinking and probably a paper.  My undeveloped thought is that perhaps the solution would be a hierarchical model:

Level 1: raw observations from e.g. GBIF
Level 2: areas classification 
Level 3: historical biogeography model

Normally we just have Level 2 as data and Level 3 as model. But if Level 2 could somehow be turned into a probabilistic model conferring a likelihood on Level 1, just as Level 3 confers a likelihood on Level 2, it might all work.

Further thoughts/discussion welcome!

Nick

Hi Nick,

Thanks for your answer ! OK, so the issue is more complicated than I
thought – I admit that I am not that deep into modelling to know how
to develop such a hierarchical model.

So for the moment, I'll just try several types of area classification
and compare them in terms of parameters and ancestral areas inferred,
knowing that I cannot compare them directly through likelihoods.

Jan
